knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=A two-dimensional matrix of expression values where rows represent samples and columns represent features (genes) ;; y=A vector of sample labels containing only -1 and 1 ;; limit=In sigFeaturePvalue, the number of top features to evaluate ;; rankedList=In sigFeaturePvalue, the vector of ranked feature indices ;; pf=In sigFeatureFrequency, a logical parameter indicating whether to use parallel processing
- alternatives: svmrfeFeatureRanking=Standard SVM-RFE algorithm (Guyon et al. 2002) which ranks features based solely on classification accuracy without considering differential significance. Use it when biological significance (p-values) of individual features is not a priority.
- when_to_use: Use this package when performing binary classification on high-dimensional transcriptomics data (e.g., microarrays) and you need to identify a subset of features that are both highly predictive and biologically/statistically significant (differentially expressed) between the two classes.
- pitfalls: Backward feature elimination is highly computationally intensive and time-consuming; users should consider pre-filtering features (e.g., using a t-test p-value threshold) or using parallel processing to reduce runtime. The input matrix x must be transposed compared to standard Bioconductor expression matrices (samples must be rows, features must be columns). Sample labels y must be strictly coded as -1 and 1.

workflows.name: significant_feature_selection_and_classification
workflows.intent: Rank features using the sigFeature algorithm, train an SVM classifier, and compare its performance and feature p-values against standard SVM-RFE.
input: expression_matrix.csv (microarray or RNA-seq expression matrix with features as rows and samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Transpose the expression matrix so samples are rows and features are columns ;; 2. Recode sample labels to -1 and 1 ;; 3. Calculate baseline p-values using sigFeaturePvalue ;; 4. Run feature selection using sigFeature or svmrfeFeatureRanking ;; 5. Train an SVM model using the top ranked features ;; 6. Predict class labels and evaluate accuracy ;; 7. Compare p-values of selected features between methods
workflows.code:
library(sigFeature)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
data(ExampleRawData, package="sigFeature")
x  <- t(assays(ExampleRawData)$counts)
y  <- colData(ExampleRawData)$sampleLabels
pvals <- sigFeaturePvalue(x,y)
#system.time(sigfeatureRankedList <- sigFeature(x, y))
data(sigfeatureRankedList)
library(e1071)
sigFeature.model=svm(x[ ,sigfeatureRankedList[1:1000]], y, 
                    type="C-classification", kernel="linear")
summary(sigFeature.model)
pred <- predict(sigFeature.model, x[ ,sigfeatureRankedList[1:1000]])
table(pred,y)
#system.time(featureRankedList <- svmrfeFeatureRanking(x, y))
data(featureRankedList)
RFE.model=svm(x[ ,featureRankedList[1:1000]], y, 
            type="C-classification", kernel="linear")
summary(RFE.model)
pred <- predict(RFE.model, x[ ,featureRankedList[1:1000]])
table(pred,y)
pvalsigFe <- sigFeaturePvalue(x, y, 100, sigfeatureRankedList)
pvalRFE   <- sigFeaturePvalue(x, y, 100, featureRankedList)

workflows.name: cross_validation_and_frequency_profiling
workflows.intent: Perform external k-fold cross-validation, rank features based on their selection frequency across folds, and estimate classification error rates.
input: expression_matrix.csv (microarray or RNA-seq expression matrix with features as rows and samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Run external cross-validation using sigFeature.enfold ;; 2. Rank features based on frequency across folds using sigFeatureFrequency ;; 3. Calculate cross-validation errors using sigCVError ;; 4. Plot validation errors using PlotErrors ;; 5. Write results using WritesigFeature
